item.title: Low-slope Lefschetz fibrations with finitely presented fundamental groups
item.description: arXiv:2611.28258v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that for any finitely presented group $G$, there exists a genus-$3k (k\in \Z)$ Lefschetz fibration over the two-sphere having slope as close as desired to $2$ and the fundamental group of the total space is isomorphic to given group $G$. These are the first examples not satisfying the slope inequality with total spaces being non-simply connected. As a corollary, by taking fiber sum of these Lefschetz fibrations with trivial genus-$3k$ Lefschetz fibration over any genus-$h(>0)$ (positive genus) surfaces, we obtain Lefschetz fibrations having slope arbitrarily close to $2$ with different fundamental groups over any genus-$h$ surface.
item.dc:creator: Tulin Altunoz, Adalet Cengel

item.title: Kleinian groups with tunnel number one
item.description: arXiv:2611.28339v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We give a structural theory for the holonomy groups of hyperbolic links with tunnel number 1 in arbitrary 3-manifolds. This is a first step towards understanding the canonical triangulations of such links, as it generalises the combinatorial structure theory of two-bridge link groups that is an input to the Sakuma--Weeks triangulation.
item.dc:creator: Alex Elzenaar

item.title: Kleinian groups generated by two elliptics of even order
item.description: arXiv:2611.28494v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $\Gamma<\mathrm{PSL}(2,\mathbb{C})$ be a non-elementary discrete group generated by two elliptics of even order, with a nontrivial relation in the corresponding free product of cyclic groups. We classify the possible compact orbifold cores of $\mathbb H^3/\Gamma$, together with their cusp data and marked meridians. They are finite meridional fillings of the two-bridge link and Heckoid models of Akiyoshi--Ohshika--Parker--Sakuma--Yoshida. Their weighted graphs have at most two standard tunnels, whose weights in the two-tunnel case are $2$ and an odd integer. The original generators are powers of primitive meridians which generate $\Gamma$, and we determine the possible meridian placements for all even orders. The groups are geometrically finite, their conformal boundary components are turnovers, and each oriented core with its cusp data determines its complete hyperbolic holonomy up to M\"obius conjugacy. The proof uses trace rigidity, dihedral surgery, half-turn symmetries, and an index-two cover.
item.dc:creator: Gaven Martin, Jeroen Schillewaert

item.title: Geometrising discrete representations in \(\textnormal{PSL}(2,\mathbb{R})\)
item.description: arXiv:2611.28570v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove the Deroin--Tholozan conjecture for discrete representations into \(\textnormal{PSL}(2,\mathbb{R})\). More precisely, we give a complete characterisation of those representations of a closed surface group with discrete image that arise as holonomies of branched hyperbolic structures. The proof combines a factorisation theorem of Rong for maps between Seifert fibred spaces with a local surgery that allows one to reinsert pinched handles while preserving the prescribed holonomy. As a consequence, we also obtain symmetric realisations on finite covers associated with normal torsion-free subgroups of the image.
item.dc:creator: Gianluca Faraco

item.title: Integral abelianizations of higher spin Torelli subgroups
item.description: arXiv:2611.28737v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We determine the integral abelianizations of the Torelli subgroups preserving an $r$-spin structure for $r\geqslant2$ and genus $g\geqslant5$. Set $n=r/\gcd(r,2)$. For a surface with one boundary component, the free rank agrees with that of the Torelli group, and the torsion subgroup is the direct sum of the usual Birman--Craggs--Johnson $2$-torsion and $\mathbb{Z}/n^2\mathbb{Z}$. For a closed surface, an $r$-spin structure exists precisely when $n\mid g-1$, and the same description holds with the additional cyclic factor replaced by $\mathbb{Z}/\gcd(n^2,g-1)\mathbb{Z}$. The additional cyclic torsion is determined by the Casson--Morita homomorphism.
item.dc:creator: Qirong Yang

item.title: Moore spaces, polyhedral products, and positive scalar curvature
item.description: arXiv:2611.29073v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Gromov conjectured that the macroscopic dimension of the universal cover of a closed $n$-manifold of positive scalar curvature is at most $n-2$. Gromov's conjecture holds for a closed spin manifold of dimension $n\geq 5$, provided that its fundamental group has property $(*)_m$, i.e., its classifying space is stably homotopy equivalent to a wedge of Moore spaces. We prove property $(*)_m$ for a large class of groups, including for instance the fundamental groups of closed hyperbolic $3$-manifolds, the commutator subgroups of right-angled Coxeter groups with low-dimensional nerves, pure braid groups, and many graph products thereof. As an additional application of independent interest, we show that there are finite-index subgroups of right-angled Artin groups that do not have property $(*)_m$ and can have arbitrary torsion in their (co)homology in any degree.
item.dc:creator: Satyanath Howladar, Lorenzo Ruffoni

item.title: Note on the extendability problem for invariant quasimorphisms for mapping class groups
item.description: arXiv:2611.29077v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this note, we study the extendability problem of invariant quasimorphisms for short exact sequences related to mapping class groups of surfaces, possibly with one boundary component or one marked point. Using a recent result of Blatz, we prove that if the genus is at least two, then every homogeneous quasimorphism on the Torelli group that is invariant by the conjugation action by the mapping class group is uniquely extendable to the whole mapping class group. Contrastingly, for the surface with one marked point whose genus is at least three, we show the existence of a homogeneous Torelli-group-invariant quasimorphism on the Johnson kernel that is not extendable.
item.dc:creator: Morimichi Kawasaki, Mitsuaki Kimura, Shuhei Maruyama, Takahiro Matsushita, Masato Mimura

item.title: Is every knot a three-way deadlock? Counterexamples and a universality conjecture for the segment number
item.description: arXiv:2611.29175v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The segment number $s(K)$ of a knot $K$ is the minimal number of arcs into which a diagram of $K$ can be cut so that, for every pair of arcs, one of them passes over the other at all of their common crossings. Every non-trivial knot satisfies $s(K)\ge 3$. In the paper introducing this invariant it was conjectured that the bridge number satisfies $b(K)\le s(K)$, and the torus knot $5_1$ was proposed as a candidate for a knot with $s(K)=4$. We show that both expectations fail: the torus knots $T(2,q)$ with $q=3,5,7,9$ have segment number three, and there is a knot $K$ with $s(K)=3$ and $b(K)\ge 4$, detected by its $3^4$ Fox $3$-colourings. We also give a knot with $s(K)=3$, signature $-6$ and $\tau=-3$, so four-dimensional invariants do not bound the segment number from below either; since $g_4(9_1)=4$, even the inequality $g_4(K)\le s(K)$ fails. Both connected sums of two trefoils, the square knot and the granny knot, also have segment number three, although a $3$-segment presentation can never be visibly composite. These results lead us to conjecture that every non-trivial knot has segment number three. We show that this is a statement about plane curves cut into three simple arcs, give a normal form in which one of the arcs is a straight segment, and report a computer census of $3$-segment presentations of prime knots, which covers all prime knots with at most eight crossings except $8_{15}$ and $8_{19}$. We also prove that every $3$-segment presentation of $K$ has at least $3u(K)$ crossings and that a minimal one has at most six bigons. All presentations are certified by exact arithmetic or combinatorial checks.
item.dc:creator: Makoto Ozawa

item.title: Unknotting number is strictly subadditive for the trefoil
item.description: arXiv:2611.29233v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A trefoil and a certain fourteen-crossing knot take four crossing changes to unknot separately and at most three together. We extend this example to infinitely many prime partners and show that the same partners give a saving for every nontrivial positive braid knot and, up to mirror, every nontrivial torus knot.
item.dc:creator: Anne Dranowski, Yura Kabkov, Daniel Tubbenhauer

item.title: Circle-Pattern Linear Systems for the Twenty Trivalent Delaunay Types of a Genus-Two Surface: Rank, Feasibility and Polytope Dimension
item.description: arXiv:2611.29848v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The hyperelliptic quotient of a closed genus-two Riemann surface is a hyperbolic sphere with six cone points of angle pi. Its Delaunay triangulation T is dual to a trivalent Voronoi graph G of one of twenty combinatorial types. For each type we study the angle system Ax = 1, x >= 0, where A is the vertex-edge incidence matrix of T and pi x_e is the angle subtended at a cone point by the Voronoi edge dual to e, equivalently the intersection angle of the two circumcircles adjacent across e. We prove that rank A = 6 for all twenty types, including the six whose triangulation has a loop, so the affine solution space always has the dimension of Teichmuller space. The polytope P = {Ax = 1, x >= 0} behaves differently. It is six-dimensional for exactly ten types, the ten Delaunay-realizable ones. For nine types it has dimension one, two or three, because non-negativity forces some wedge angles to vanish, and for the type of signature (2,2,2,2,8,8) it is empty. We show that five of the nine and the empty type never occur as Delaunay triangulations, and that the other four occur only as triangulations of non-trivalent Delaunay decompositions. Every vertex of every P is half-integral, as for fractional perfect matching polytopes. For the ten full-dimensional types every facet x_e = 0 lies at an edge where the Whitehead move is admissible, though not conversely, and the move identifies the facets of the two polytopes; these identifications pair the facet orbits of the ten cells under their automorphism groups. The free unfolding of the gluing grows at rate about 7.093. All finite statements are checked by an independent program, and the rank, infeasibility, forced coordinates, dimensions, vertices and facets are verified in Lean 4.
item.dc:creator: Armando Rodado Amaris

item.title: H(n)-Gordian graphs of knotoids and their quotients: Gromov hyperbolicity
item.description: arXiv:2611.30056v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we study $H(n)$-moves on knotoid diagrams and the corresponding $H(n)$-Gordian graphs. We establish that the $H(n)$-Gordian graphs of knotoids are not Gromov hyperbolic. We also consider quotient graphs of the $H(n)$-Gordian graph of knotoids by the following knotoid invariants: the height of a knotoid, the span of the affine index polynomial, the $y$-span and $z$-span of the invariant $H_K(t, y, z)$, and the span of the Jones polynomial. We prove that in all these cases, the quotient graphs are Gromov hyperbolic.
item.dc:creator: M. Alikbarov, A. Vesnin

item.title: A complete knot invariant from grid diagrams
item.description: arXiv:2611.30095v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Using grid diagrams, we define an infinite graph associated to each knot type. We prove that the isomorphism class of this grid graph is a complete invariant of the knot, up to mirroring. Even more, we prove that algorithmically determinable finite parts of this graph are enough to determine the knot type.
item.dc:creator: Agnese Barbensi, Daniele Celoria, Lavender Marshall, Finn Thompson

item.title: Eigendecomposition for instantons via infinity-category
item.description: arXiv:2611.30364v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Suppose $L$ is a framed link in a balanced sutured manifold $(M, \gamma)$. We construct a link spectral sequence in sutured instanton homology. For properly embedded surfaces in $M$ disjoint from $L$, we refine the spectral sequence to preserve the induced multi-grading. We use $\infty$-categories to encode homotopical information from instanton theory. In particular, we obtain a simultaneous eigendecomposition of homotopy-coherently commutative operators on a chain complex or a hypercube complex. As the algebraic foundation for subsequent work of the second author and collaborators, we construct the mixed hypercube by combining the hypercubes of positive and negative bypass maps. This construction is compatible with the eigendecomposition associated with the surface multi-grading on sutured instanton homology.
item.dc:creator: Longke Tang, Fan Ye

item.title: A corank one Lipschitz normally embedded surface in $\mathbb{R}^4$ with non-trivial link
item.description: arXiv:2611.30544v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We show that the knot-triviality theorem for Lipschitz normally embedded (LNE) corank one surface singularities in $\mathbb{R}^4$ proved by Birbrair, Mendes and Nu\~no-Ballesteros (2018) does not generalize unrestrictedly. More precisely, we exhibit a polynomial map germ $F:(\mathbb{R}^2,0)\to(\mathbb{R}^4,0)$ of corank one at the origin, with isolated singularity and $2$-jet $(x,0,0,0)$, whose image $X=F(\mathbb{R}^2)$ is LNE at the origin, yet its link is the granny knot $T\#T$, and hence non-trivial. The example is obtained via a general uniform-degree homogenization procedure applied to a known polynomial parametrization of the trefoil knot. We also give a finitely $\mathcal A$-determined polynomial realization with the same LNE and knot properties.
item.dc:creator: L. Birbrair, Rodrigo Mendes, J. J. Nu\~no-Ballesteros

item.title: Spherical CR uniformization for 7 links
item.description: arXiv:2611.30797v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider subgroups in $PU(2,1)$ generated by three involutions $I_1,I_2,I_3$ such that $I_2I_3$ has order $p$ and the elements $I_1I_2$, $I_2I_3$, $I_1I_3I_2I_3$ are all in the same conjugacy class of $PU(2,1)$. We show that these groups are discrete whenever $I_1I_2$ and $I_1I_2I_3$ are non-elliptic and we study the orbifolds at infinity. In addition, we show that for $3 \leq p \leq 9$ the complement of a symmetric cyclic chain of $p$ simple links admits a spherical CR uniformization.
item.dc:creator: Julio Quijas-Aceves

item.title: A hyperbolic 7-manifold that fibers over the circle
item.description: arXiv:2611.30871v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We construct an explicit orientable finite-volume hyperbolic $7$-manifold $M$ that fibers over the circle. The manifold is tessellated by $256$ copies of the right-angled hyperbolic polytope $P^7$ and has $252$ cusps. The fiber is the interior of a compact aspherical $6$-manifold whose boundary consists of $256$ five-dimensional tori. The fibration comes from a Bestvina-Brady Morse function on the Davis complex. Bestvina-Brady theory shows that the kernel of the associated character is finitely presented. A perturbation argument over the integral Novikov ring shows that the infinite cyclic cover is finitely dominated. Farrell's fibering theorem, together with the vanishing of the Whitehead group, then gives the fibration.
item.dc:creator: Lizi Guo

item.title: On the space of left orders on the groups $QI(\mathbb{R}_+),\,QI(\mathbb{R}_+)/H \text{ and }G_\infty$
item.description: arXiv:2611.31188v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce the notion of a left order on a group with a certain specification of signs for the elements of a subset. We obtain an equivalent criterion for the existence of such a left order and apply it to obtain a new proof of the fact that any of the groups $QI(\mathbb{R}_+),\,QI(\mathbb{R}_+)/H,\,G_\infty$ admits infinitely many non-Conradian left orders. We introduce the notion of separation of free subsemigroups of a left ordered group by its left translation induced actions on a point in the group and show that the above three groups admit such left orders. We also construct a subset of the set of left orders on any of the three groups, show the subset is a perfect set and give a new proof of the fact that the sets of the left orders on these three groups are uncountable.
item.dc:creator: Prateep Chakraborty

item.title: A filtered basis for Haiman ideals
item.description: arXiv:2611.28264v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Given the polynomial ring $R=\mathbb{C}[x_1, \dots, x_n, y_1, \dots, y_n]$, we consider the Haiman ideal $J(d)$ of polynomials that vanish to order $d$ on the diagonals. We define a rotational order on monomials and use it to construct a filtration on $J(d)$ and a bigraded, homogeneous, free $\mathbb{C}[\mathbf{y}]$-basis compatible with this filtration. This gives a new independent proof that $J(d)$ is free over $y$'s. We also discuss the connections between this filtration and triply-graded link homology.
item.dc:creator: Joshua P. Turner

item.title: Computing pro-$p$ Closures of Finitely Generated Subgroups of Closed Orientable Surface Groups
item.description: arXiv:2611.28412v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $\Gamma_g$ be the fundamental group of a closed orientable surface of genus $g\geq2$, and let $p$ be a prime. For every finitely generated subgroup $H\leq\Gamma_g$ we give an algorithm which, given any finite generating set of $H$ by words in a standard generating set, outputs a finite set of words in the same alphabet that generates the pro-$p$ closure of $H$. This extends the computation of pro-$p$ closures in free groups by Ribes-Zalesskii and Margolis-Sapir-Weil.
item.dc:creator: Zheng Dang, Jianchun Wu

item.title: Exotic Universal Covers and Free Cyclic Actions from the Cartwright-Steger Surface
item.description: arXiv:2611.28956v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: For every $m\geq2$, we construct a closed minimal symplectic four-manifold with fundamental group $\Z/m$, Euler characteristic $35$, and signature $1$. The construction is a genus-five symplectic sum of a blowup of the regular fourfold Cartwright-Steger cover and a cyclic Akhmedov-Park manifold. The gluing identifies the homomorphisms from the two surface groups to $\Z/m$. The universal cover is minimal symplectic and is homeomorphic but not diffeomorphic to $(18m-1)\CP\#(17m-1)\CPb$. It admits a free symplectic action of $\Z/m$. Intermediate quotients give examples with fundamental group $\Z/n$ and characteristic numbers $(e,\sigma)=(35k,k)$ for every $n\geq2$ and $k\geq1$. Using the same Cartwright-Steger summand, we also construct, for every $m\geq2$, a minimal symplectic four-manifold with fundamental group $\Z/m$, Euler characteristic $31$, and signature $1$, whose minimal symplectic universal cover is an exotic copy of $(16m-1)\CP\#(15m-1)\CPb$ with a free symplectic $\Z/m$-action.
item.dc:creator: Anar Akhmedov, B. Doug Park, S\"{u}meyra Sakall{\i}, Sai-Kee Yeung

item.title: M\"obius Fusion Algebra
item.description: arXiv:2611.29234v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Given a pseudo-unitary modular tensor category $\mathcal{C}$ with an anti-monoidal involution $\mathsf{P}$, we define a generally non-commutative algebra from this data, which we call the M\"obius fusion algebra $\mathfrak{M}$ of $(\mathcal{C},\mathsf{P})$, in terms of ribbon graphs drawn on the M\"obius band, where the orientation-reversal of the M\"obius band acts on the graphs by $\mathsf{P}$. We show that this algebra is semisimple, and give a formula for the dimensions of its simple modules, in terms of the modular $S$-matrix of $\mathcal{C}$ and a certain set of quantities extracted from the action of $\mathsf{P}$. This formula is expected to play the role of a non-orientable analogue of the Verlinde formula, in the context of Reshetikhin-Turaev-type topological quantum field theories on non-orientable manifolds.
item.dc:creator: Ippo Orii, Yuji Tachikawa

item.title: Form of Words in Free Products with scl 1/12
item.description: arXiv:2611.29812v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $G = *_\lambda G_\lambda$ be a free product of groups and let $g\in G$ be any element not conjugate into any free factor and not conjugate to its inverse. Then $\mathrm{scl}(g) \ge \frac{1}{12}$ and $\mathrm{scl}(g) = \frac{1}{12}$ if and only if $g$ is a product of an element of order $2$ and an element of order $3$. In particular, this classifies all elements in $G = \mathrm{PSL}(2, \mathbb{Z})$ with $\mathrm{scl}_G(g) = \frac{1}{12}$.
item.dc:creator: Jacob Strietelmeier

item.title: Frobenius $2$-algebras and $R$-matrices
item.description: arXiv:2611.29898v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In this paper, introducing Frobenius $2$-algebras, which are categorical generalizations of Frobenius algebras, we show that every Frobenius $2$-algebra determines an $R$-matrix satisfying the Yang-Baxter equation in the monoidal category of endomorphisms of its underlying object. Moreover, we illustrate this construction through three examples: a pair of objects in a braided monoidal category, a Hopf algebra with invertible antipode, and representations of the Heisenberg double of a finite-dimensional Hopf algebra. In particular, in the third example, we recover Kashaev's construction of the universal $R$-matrix. Thus, our construction provides a categorical generalization of Kashaev's construction.
item.dc:creator: Hibiki Shibuya, Yuji Terashima

item.title: Strong convergence of uniformly random permutation representations of surface groups
item.description: arXiv:2504.08988v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $\Gamma$ be the fundamental group of a closed orientable surface of genus at least two. Consider the composition of a uniformly random element of $\mathrm{Hom}(\Gamma,S_n)$ with the $(n-1)$-dimensional irreducible representation of $S_n$. We prove the strong convergence in probability as $n\to\infty$ of this sequence of random representations to the regular representation of $\Gamma$. As a consequence, for any closed orientable hyperbolic surface $X$, with probability tending to one as $n\to\infty$, a uniformly random degree-$n$ covering space of $X$ has near optimal relative spectral gap --- ignoring the eigenvalues that arise from the base surface $X$. To do so, we show that the polynomial method of proving strong convergence can be extended beyond rational settings. To meet the requirements of this extension we prove two new kinds of results. First, we show there are effective polynomial approximations of expected values of traces of elements of $\Gamma$ under random homomorphisms to $S_{n}$. Secondly, we estimate the growth rates of probabilities that a finitely supported random walk on $\Gamma$ is a proper power after a given number of steps.
item.dc:creator: Michael Magee, Doron Puder, Ramon van Handel

item.title: Independence of homogeneous GKM manifolds and symmetric spaces
item.description: arXiv:2602.07734v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $G/H$ be a simply connected homogeneous space of maximal rank. Then the maximal torus $T$-action on $G/H$ equips it with a structure of a Goresky-Kottwitz-MacPherson (GKM) manifold. We call the $T$-action $j$-independent if any $i\leq j$ pairwise distinct isotropy weights at a fixed point are linearly independent. Using weighted graphs, we show that the maximal independence of $G/H$ is $2$, $3$ or $n=\dim T$, and that the cases of $3$ or $n=\dim T$ correspond to some symmetric spaces of rank $>2$ by using the Lie bracket structure at the tangent space at identity coset. We classify all $4$-independent homogeneous spaces by studying the $3$- and $4$-cycles in the matroid of the respective root subsystem complement using Borel-de Siebenthal and Cartan classification results. In the classical $G$ cases our case study of maximal independence relies on signed weighted graphs, following the classical methods of Zaslavsky and Harari. In the exceptional simply laced $G$ cases we either present a $3$-cycle, or prove that there is none by reducing them only to those having a form $x+y=z$ for positive roots $x,y,z$ and find an affine hyperplane containing the respective root complement. As a corollary, using the results of Ayzenberg and Masuda, the lower-degree reduced rational cohomology groups of the orbit space $T\backslash G/H$ vanish.
item.dc:creator: Shintaro Kuroki, Grigory Solomadin

item.title: Fixed-parameter tractable computation of Reshetikhin--Turaev knot polynomials via tensor networks
item.description: arXiv:2606.29662v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We give a thorough analysis of the time complexity of computing Reshetikhin--Tuareg knot polynomials via tensor contractions on the associated tensor networks, showing that the computation is fixed-parameter tractable with respect to a parameter at most linear in the tree-width of the input knot diagram. In particular, this gives a simpler proof to the sub-exponential bound $e^{O(\sqrt{n})}$ for the time complexity of computing any Reshetikhin--Turaev knot polynomial. We present along with this paper, in SnapPy, the first general-purpose implementation of this algorithm, which computes any Reshetikhin--Turaev knot polynomial given its $R$-matrix and ribbon element. We stress the remarkable efficiency of our implementation by demonstrating that: (1) our implementation is several orders of magnitude faster than existing packages on computing the colored Jones polynomial; (2) our implementation is able to compute the Jones polynomial of (i) census knots with large width and over 200 crossings and (ii) some generic random knots with over 2000 crossings, in several hours using less than 10GB RAM, whereas Regina is not able to compute the Jones polynomial of these knots within a memory constraint of 160GB.
item.dc:creator: Shana Yunsheng Li

item.title: Montesinos Knots with Delta-Unknotting Number One
item.description: arXiv:2609.39565v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The $\Delta$-unknotting number for a knot is defined as the minimum number of $\Delta$-moves needed to deform the knot into the trivial knot. In this paper, we discuss Montesinos knots whose $\Delta$-unknotting number is equal to one. We propose a conjectural characterization of Montesinos knots with $\Delta$-unknotting number one and provide examples admitting distinct $\Delta$-moves, each of which deforms the knot into the trivial knot. Furthermore, we present examples illustrating the relationship between the locations of $\Delta$-moves and $X$-moves for knots with $u^{\Delta}(K) = 1$, considering separately the cases $u(K) = 1$ and $u(K) = 2$.
item.dc:creator: Kazumichi Nakamura

item.title: On the connectedness of a minimizing cluster's boundary
item.description: arXiv:2512.15403v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We verify that an isoperimetric minimizing cluster on a simply connected homogeneous Riemannian manifold with at most one end always has connected boundary. In particular, the boundary of a single-bubble isoperimetric minimizer on such manifolds must be connected, and hence all isoperimetric sets and their complements must be connected. This is demonstrably false without the simple connectedness assumption or the restriction on the number of ends.
item.dc:creator: Emanuel Milman, Joe Neeman

item.title: Spectral Dehn Functions: Hyperbolicity, Filling Geometry and Diffusion
item.description: arXiv:2604.09014v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We show that Dirichlet eigenvalues of van Kampen diagrams can distinguish groups whose Dehn functions have the same order. The Dehn function bounds the least filling area in terms of word length. We use the random walk on the faces, stopped at the exterior. For each null word we take the infimum, over its fillings, of the reciprocal of the first Dirichlet eigenvalue, then maximize over words of length at most $n$. We call this the spectral Dehn function. Its coarse growth is a quasi-isometry invariant for presentations whose generators form a word ball and whose relators are all null words of length at most three. In such a presentation of $\mathbb{Z}^2$, the boundary word of a square can have a filling with more faces and a larger first eigenvalue than any of its least-area fillings. For two groups with quartic Dehn functions, it is at most $Cn^4$ for one and at least $cn^6/(\log n)^2$ for the other. The spectral Dehn function is bounded exactly for word-hyperbolic groups. For other finitely presented groups it grows at least as fast as $n^2/(\log n)^2$. In these presentations the bound is sharp for non-hyperbolic automatic groups and for non-hyperbolic groups acting properly and cocompactly by isometries on proper geodesic Lipschitz $1$-connected spaces. For the face walk we maximize the expected absorption time over starting faces. In these classes its supremum over least-area fillings of cyclically reduced null words of length at most $n$ has order $n^2$. Taking the infimum over all fillings of each null word before maximizing over words of length at most $n$ gives order $n^2/\log n$ in these presentations. Under a quadratic isoperimetric inequality, every non-hyperbolic group has, for each sufficiently large $n$, a null word of length at most $n$ whose least-area fillings have, for the face and vertex walks, $j$th Dirichlet eigenvalue of order $j/n^2$ for $1\le j\le cn^2$.
item.dc:creator: Mayukh Mukherjee

item.title: Self-intersecting sections of polar actions on simply connected manifolds
item.description: arXiv:2610.12446v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We construct a polar action of $\mathrm{SU}(3)$ on a closed simply connected $11$-manifold with a compact three-dimensional section that is not injectively immersed. The section is injective over the regular part and has two distinct local branches along a singular stratum. All isotropy groups are connected, and all orbits are simply connected. This gives a negative answer to the injectivity question raised by Grove and Ziller.
item.dc:creator: Stephan Wiesendorf

item.title: Virtually solvable groups with balanced presentations
item.description: arXiv:2611.21875v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We show that if $G$ is a virtually solvable group with finite Hirsch length and such that $\beta_2(G;\mathbb{Q})\leq\beta=\beta_1(G;\mathbb{Q})$ then $\beta\leq3$. This sharpens bounds on the Betti numbers of 3-manifolds which embed in $S^4$ with the fundamental groups of each complementary region virtually solvable and of finite Hirsch length.
item.dc:creator: Jonathan A. Hillman

item.title: Generalizing the Gaster--Loustau Theorem via Generalized Discrete Markov Spectra
item.description: arXiv:2611.23868v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We realize generalized Markov numbers (GM numbers) for arbitrary $k_1,k_2,k_3\in\ZZ_{\ge0}$ as $\lambda$-lengths of essential simple ideal arcs based at a distinguished cusp of a hyperbolic orbifold constructed from local monodromy matrices. The McShane identity of Tan--Wong--Zhang on this orbifold yields a summation identity with multiplicities for the gaps between the associated Lagrange constants and their limiting value, together with a summation inequality that counts each distinct value once. These results extend the summation identity and inequality of Gaster and Loustau to generalized Markov numbers.
item.dc:creator: Yasuaki Gyoda
